newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-New Australia wool stockpile sales law passed.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-New Australia wool stockpile sales law passed.

text.p: The Australian Senate on Thursday passed the Wool International Amendment Bill to provide for changes to statutory authority Wool International's (WI) disposal schedule from the Australian wool stockpile.
The new disposal schedule sets minimum sales of 135,000 bales a quarter from January 1 1997, reducing to 90,000 bales from July 1 1997.
Maximum sales of 350,000 bales a quarter apply from January 1, 1997.
Previous arrangements required quarterly sales of 182,000 to 192,000 bales a quarter.

Senator David Brownhill, parliamentary secretary to the Minister for Primary Industries and Energy, said in a statement that greater flexibility would be provided WI in the selling of the stockpile, with benefits able to flow on to the industry.
Woolgrowers had complained that the current sales schedule provided too much wool when the market was weak, exacerbating weakness at auction sales, and too little when demand was strong.
Australia's wool stockpile has recently fallen just below the two million bales mark, down from the peak of 4.72 million bales in 1991. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
